title: How do we divide two powers of the same base?
description: Two to the power one hundred is divided by two to the power twenty five by cancelling twos, and the video also asks why the base cannot be zero. Keeko doubts whether the exponents are divided or taken away.
teaching_notes: One idea: dividing powers of one base cancels factors, so the exponents are taken away. Watch for students who divide the exponents, and for students who miss that a base of zero would mean dividing by zero.

source: Write 2 to the power 100 ÷ 2 to the power 25 as a power of 2, and explain why the rule needs n ≠ 0.
video_script.why: A learner generalises the cancelling of twos to any two powers of one base, and sees why the base cannot be zero.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question of two to the power one hundred divided by two to the power twenty five
video_script.anchor: two to the power one hundred written as a fraction, with the twos above and below the bar
video_script.wrong_move: divides the exponents one hundred by twenty five instead of taking them away
video_script.payoff_line: One hundred twos over twenty five twos leave seventy five twos

final_answer.value: 2 to the power 75; the base cannot be 0 because we cannot divide by 0
final_answer.spoken: two to the power seventy five; the base cannot be zero because we cannot divide by zero

maths_rules: each of the 25 factors below cancels one above
n^a / n^b = n^(a - b), n is not 0, a > b
0^25 = 0, and dividing by 0 is not defined
video_script.design: One idea: cancelling twos takes exponents away. Wrong idea: divide the exponents. The twos sit above and below a bar and the cancelled ones fade; the final power only appears at the answer.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>We have two to the power one hundred, divided by two to the power twenty five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write the answer as a power of two.

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 2^100 / 2^25 as a fraction: 100 twos above the bar, 25 twos below it

marks.twos: 2^100 is spelled out as a long row of 2s multiplied
marks.frac: the division becomes a fraction bar
marks.rows: 100 twos sit above the bar and 25 twos below it

narration: <bookmark mark='twos'/>Two to the power one hundred means one hundred twos multiplied together.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>We can write the division as a fraction.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>The one hundred twos go above the bar, and the twenty five twos go below it.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two to the power one hundred divided by two to the power twenty five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the result as a power of 2; why the base cannot be 0

marks.find: the words result as a power of 2 and why the base cannot be 0 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find this as a power of two, and see why the base cannot be zero.

beats.on_screen: count the twos: 100 above the bar, 25 below it
narration: <bookmark mark='above'/>Step one, count the twos. Above the bar there are one hundred twos.
<bookmark mark='below'/>Below the bar there are twenty five twos.

beats.on_screen: each of the 25 twos below cancels one 2 above; 100 - 25 = 75 twos are left

marks.cancel: the 25 twos below fade together with 25 twos above

narration: <bookmark mark='cancel'/>Step two, cancel the twos, because each two below cancels one two above.
<bookmark mark='left'/>One hundred take away twenty five leaves seventy five twos.

beats.on_screen: rule: n^a / n^b = n^(a - b), n is not 0, a > b; here 2^(100 - 25)

marks.say: n^a / n^b = n^(a - b) with n is not 0 and a > b is written
marks.here: 2^(100 - 25) is written under the rule, the result is left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, write what we found as a rule.
<bookmark mark='say'/>For any base n that is not zero, dividing two powers of n takes the exponents away.
<bookmark mark='here'/>Here the base is two, and the exponent is one hundred minus twenty five.

beats.on_screen: base 0: the divisor 0^25 = 0, and dividing by 0 is not defined

marks.stop: a stop sign marks dividing by 0 as not defined

narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Step four, try the base zero. Zero to the power twenty five is zero.
<bookmark mark='stop'/>The divisor would be zero, and we cannot divide by zero.

marks.ans: 2^75 is written, with the base cannot be 0 beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>One hundred twos over twenty five twos leave seventy five twos.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The answer is two to the power seventy five. The base cannot be zero, because we cannot divide by zero.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 100 / 25 = 4, so 2^4, struck out; 2^10 / 2^5 leaves five 2s beside it

marks.fix: ten 2s over five 2s are drawn and five 2s are left
marks.all: the bubble is struck out and 10 - 5 = 5 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is two to the power four, from dividing one hundred by twenty five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But try ten twos over five twos. Cancelling leaves five twos, while dividing ten by five gives only two.
<bookmark mark='all'/>The exponents are taken away, not divided.
